road.title: Where you went
road.description: A tall, folded person wearing a waistcoat the colour of old tea, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Ignatius is a Returned Explorer and went somewhere once, came back, and has measured everyone else's trips against it ever since.

character.name: Ignatius Fiddlewick
character.description: A tall, folded person wearing a waistcoat the colour of old tea, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Ignatius is a Returned Explorer and went somewhere once, came back, and has measured everyone else's trips against it ever since.

npc.narrative: It is mezzogiorno, and you cross the piazza of the Reluctant Green under a clear cielo and a sole that has plainly been told to behave. On a panchina sits Ignatius Fiddlewick, holding his cappello like a small, unreliable witness. Beyond him the strada goes on, and a single albero leans in the manner of someone listening.
npc.native: Buongiorno! Ieri sono andato al ponte da solo, e sono partito all'alba. It rained nowhere, which I found suspicious. I am certain we have met, and I apologise for being wrong. Tell me about your last trip: dove sei andato tu, e con chi?

player: Sono andato a Vienna con mia sorella.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer: you told Ignatius you went to Vienna with your sister, in correct Italian. Next time, add when you left.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you said where you went, using the past tense correctly.
You didn't say when you left yet. Tell Ignatius at what time or on which day you set off, and he will ask you again later.
Well done: you said who you went with.

openObjectives.prompt: Ignatius keeps a book of departures, and you are not in it. Tell Ignatius when you left, using Italian.
Tell Ignatius who you went with, or that you went alone, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Ignatius folds his mappa into a smaller, sadder mappa. Under the clear cielo, he studies your faccia with the dubbio of a man who has almost placed it. A single nuvola, far off, is ignored per principio.
npc.native: Vienna, you say. Che viaggio lungo! My bridge was nearer, and the disappointment correspondingly smaller. Quando sei partito per Vienna?

player: Sono partito lunedì mattina, molto presto.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely, clear answer: you told Ignatius you left on Monday morning, very early. Next, tell him about who you travelled with.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you said when you left, using "Sono partito" correctly.
This one still needs you to tell Ignatius who you went with, or that you went alone; he will ask again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Ignatius who you went with, or that you went alone, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Ignatius inspects the ponte like a man auditing a disappointment. The cielo is clear, which he takes personally. From his cappotto he draws a piccolo quaderno, mostly crossed out, and licks a matita.
npc.native: Lunedì mattina, molto presto! Io parto sempre con un ombrello, anche quando il cielo è chiaro. Nobody has ever thanked an umbrella, but it is never wrong. Ti piace partire così presto?

player: No, non mi piace! Ma il treno era alle sei.

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice, clear Italian: you said you don't like leaving early and that the train was at six. Next time, add who you travelled with, or that you went alone.

objectiveResults.feedback: This answer doesn't say who you went with or that you went alone, so try telling Ignatius that in Italian.

npc.narrative: The sole is alto over the strada, and the cielo has nothing to hide, which Ignatius takes personally. He tips his ombrello at you, as one salutes an old amico or a ponte. Then he lifts his borsa and goes, piano piano.
npc.native: Il treno alle sei: allora capisco. Io viaggio sempre da solo, ma oggi vado con un ombrello. Buon viaggio a te e a tua sorella. Arrivederci!
npc.translation: The train at six: then I understand, and I call that a crime against the morning. I always travel alone, but today I go with an umbrella, which is as much company as I trust. Have a good trip, you and your sister, and may Vienna be kinder than Monday was. Goodbye!

player: Grazie! Vienna è la mia città preferita.

npc.narrative: Il sole stands straight overhead and the cielo has nothing to declare. Ignatius leans on his ombrello, closed for once, and studies you with the polite certainty of a man who has seen you before, forse in a better hat. Un gatto on the wall decides against the whole matter.
npc.native: Vienna è la tua città preferita! Cities have cellars, you see, and cellars worry me. Mia zia non vuole un pozzo in casa: she says a hole is a door, and everybody knows where that door goes. Che cosa ti piace di Vienna?
npc.translation: Vienna is your favourite city! Cities have cellars, you see, and cellars worry me. My aunt does not want a well in the house: she says a hole is a door, and everybody knows where that door goes. What do you like about Vienna?
